correctness.rationale: The normalized monomials sqrt(k+1) z^k diagonalize the radial positive compression by angular orthogonality. Squared radius s has uniform normalized area density, and s=t/(1+t) maps the first Cantor-stage t bands exactly onto S=[0,a]∪[b,c] with 0<a<b<c<1 for all R>0. The eigenvalues are a^{k+1}+c^{k+1}−b^{k+1}; the rational simplification for L=a+c−b was independently checked symbolically. To verify strict comparison, the sign of H(b)=a−bL is positive iff a/b>(c−b)/(1−b). The two ratios are (2R+3)/(2(R+3)) and R/(3(R+1)); cross multiplying gives the strictly positive difference 4R²+9R+9. The distribution discrepancy H(s)=|S∩[0,s]|−Ls is linear between endpoints, increases inside S, decreases outside, has H(0)=H(1)=0 and H(b)>0. Hence H(s)>0 for every 0<s<1. Integrating H' against (k+1)s^k gives λ₀−λ_k=k(k+1)∫H(s)s^{k−1}ds>0 for all k≥1. The positive diagonal operator consequently has norm L, and the equality condition for a unit vector is precisely support on the constant basis element. Since λ_k≤a^{k+1}+c^{k+1}→0, the top eigenvalue is also isolated. This proves the all-real-R and all-degree statements; the exact-rational frozen verifier was inspected, not run, and its finite checks are not used as a proof.

originality.rationale: The primary Bergman Cantor theorem supplies the exact beta-prime spectral representation and norm bounds, not strict comparison of modes. The strongest indexed vacuum theorem uses critical dilation at even depths 2m≥4, not the first stage at arbitrary dilation. Exact indexed two-component comparisons use different families and can prefer high modes. Thus the distinct supported claim is the strict first-stage maximizing-mode law, exact norm and equality case for all positive R, not eigenvalue integration or broader priority.
residual_risks: The bounded catalogue and accessible primary-paper comparisons do not rule out an equivalent first-stage statement or a stronger all-parameter radial-ordering theorem under different terminology.

value.rationale: The first disconnected iterate of the published hyperbolic Cantor model is a natural test case, not an arbitrary cutoff. The finding determines a sharp norm and all extremizers across the full dilation axis. Generic two-band masks can select nonconstant modes and the prior exact integrals and two-sided norm bounds do not mechanically settle the maximization. The cumulative criterion is a short but substantive solution to that specific spectral comparison, without claiming all stages or all radial symbols.
